How coral reefs recover after bleaching

Coral bleaching happens when water stays too warm for several weeks and corals expel the algae that feed them.

Researchers who followed reefs for ten years found that most bleached corals can recover if the water cools within a few months.

Recovery is fastest on reefs with clear water, plenty of fish that graze on seaweed, and little pollution from the land.

Share this: Facebook Twitter Email

Repeated bleaching events, however, leave too little time between heat waves, and reefs then lose their most fragile species first.

The study suggests that cutting local pollution can buy reefs time while global emissions are reduced.
